A well-planned vegan diet that includes reliable sources of vitamin B12 and vitamin D can meet nutrient needs during pregnancy, and several scientific societies endorse plant-based diets in pregnancy [d2,d5,d7]. However, national medical bodies such as Belgium’s Royal Academy of Medicine advise against vegan diets for pregnant women due to risks of deficiencies and irreversible harm if not properly monitored [d1]. Some sources also caution that restrictive vegan keto diets are not suitable during pregnancy and that careful planning and supplementation are essential [d3,d6]. Given these conflicting expert opinions, pregnant women should consult a qualified healthcare provider to assess individual risks and benefits before choosing a vegan diet [d1,d2,d5,d7].
